title_en: Shanghai Panqi Trading Co., Ltd. v. Panqi Industry (Dalian) Co., Ltd. — dispute over agency contract
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 410 of the Contract Law, the principal or the agent may terminate the agency contract at any time. If losses are caused to the other party by the termination, compensation shall be paid, unless the termination is attributable to reasons not imputable to the terminating party. full_text_en:
Shanghai Panqi Trading Co., Ltd. v. Panqi Industry (Dalian) Co., Ltd. — dispute over entrustment contract

【Ruling Summary】

According to Article 410 of the Contract Law, the principal or the agent may terminate the entrustment contract at any time. If the termination causes losses to the other party, compensation shall be made unless the termination is not attributable to the terminating party. However, the civil liability for damages arising from termination of an entrustment contract is different from civil liability arising from intentional breach of contract. The scope of liability for the former is limited to direct losses caused to the other party and does not include the other party's expected benefits.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment
(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 143

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): Shanghai Panqi Trading Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 77, Eshan Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Liang Chongxuan, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Li Xiaolin, lawyer at Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Panqi Industry (Dalian) Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 5, Jinzhou Street, Dalian Development Zone, Liaoning Province.
Legal representative: Morikubo Yuji, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Shen Zejing, lawyer at Beijing Haotian Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Lu Jincheng, lawyer at Beijing Haotian Law Firm.

Appellant Shanghai Panqi Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Panqi) filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2003) Liao Min San He Chu Zi No. 34 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court in the case of dispute over entrustment contract with appellee Panqi Industry (Dalian) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dalian Panqi). In accordance with the law, this Court formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Xu Ruibai, Judge Zhang Shuming, and Acting Judge Zhang Xuemei to hear the case. Court Clerk Pan Yongfeng served as the recorder. The hearing of this case has now concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial that:

In July 2000, Morikubo Yuji, the legal representative of Japanese Panqi Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Japanese Panqi) (who also served as the legal representative of Dalian Panqi), after consultations with Liang Chongxuan, signed the "Decision on Building Panqi China Marketing Network and Establishing Shanghai Panqi" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision"). The Decision provided for the establishment of Shanghai Panqi, which would be responsible for building, operating, and managing the Panqi China marketing network. It confirmed that Shanghai Panqi was a member of the Panqi Group and the sole sales representative agency of the Panqi Group in the China region (excluding Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau). Shanghai Panqi was a limited liability company registered in China, operating as an independent legal entity, independently managing its operations, bearing its own losses, and retaining its own profits. The Panqi Group would supply products to Shanghai Panqi at the most favorable prices. The Decision also stipulated matters concerning business operations and company management. Subsequently, Morikubo Yuji and Liang Chongxuan executed a "Letter of Entrustment" (hereinafter referred to as the "Letter"), which provided that Liang Chongxuan was entrusted to represent Japanese Panqi and its affiliated enterprises in building, managing, and operating the sales institutions and channels of the Panqi Group's marketing network in the China region (excluding Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau); to establish, operate, and manage Shanghai Panqi and other relevant sales institutions; and to be entrusted to serve as a shareholder, director, and chairman of the board of Shanghai Panqi. The scope of authority, responsibilities, and specific matters would be governed by the Decision. Japanese Panqi was responsible for coordinating and instructing all departments and affiliated enterprises within the Panqi Group to enter into business relationship agreements with Shanghai Panqi. The Letter also provided that the trustee unconditionally accepted the revocation of the entrustment by the principal.

On July 28 of the same year, Shanghai Panqi was established upon approval by the administrative department for industry and commerce, as a limited liability company with a registered capital of RMB 1,000,000, of which Liang Chongxuan contributed RMB 900,000 and Bi Chunsheng contributed RMB 100,000. Liang Chongxuan served as the legal representative. The company's business scope included: molds and components, mechanical parts, hardware tools, metal products (excluding those subject to special approval), plastic products, and chemical raw materials (excluding hazardous materials).

In August of the same year, Shanghai Panqi and Dalian Panqi signed a "Business Agreement" (hereinafter referred to as the "Agreement"), confirming the following terms regarding Dalian Panqi's entrustment of Shanghai Panqi for sales in the China region (excluding Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau):

- Both parties mutually confirmed that they were members of the Panqi Group and shared common interests and responsibilities in the business of Panqi Industry.
- Dalian Panqi, as the manufacturing base of the Panqi Group in China, had the responsibility to supply Shanghai Panqi with the required products in accordance with Panqi Group standards, with respect to quality, time, and quantity.
- Shanghai Panqi, as the sales representative agency of the Panqi Group in the China region, had the responsibility to explore and develop the market for the products of the Panqi Group and Dalian Panqi in the China region.
- Dalian Panqi entrusted Shanghai Panqi to sell its manufactured products in the China region and agreed not to entrust or establish other sales institutions or channels. If necessary, Dalian Panqi was required to negotiate an agreement with Shanghai Panqi in advance.
- Shanghai Panqi was responsible for building, managing, and operating sales institutions and channels, and could purchase products from other manufacturers for sale as needed based on customer requirements.
- Dalian Panqi would supply products at the most favorable prices and would provide and transfer to Shanghai Panqi free of charge the sales rights, trademark rights, and other intangible assets in the China region. Shanghai Panqi guaranteed the proper use of such sales rights, trademarks, and intangible assets.
- The agreement was valid for 20 years, from September 1, 2000 to August 31, 2020.

After the signing of the Agreement, the parties commenced cooperation. Shanghai Panqi placed orders with Dalian Panqi for various molds and accessories via fax or email and conducted sales activities. Shanghai Panqi also promoted Dalian Panqi's products and developed the market through advertising, brochures, exhibitions, and trade fairs, and successively established sales outlets in Guangdong, Qingdao, Suzhou, Kunshan, Tianjin, Hangzhou, and other locations, forming a sales network of a certain scale. The parties did not expressly agree on the settlement period for the purchase price. As of April 2002, Shanghai Panqi had an outstanding payment of RMB 5,916,866.41 to Dalian Panqi, but Dalian Panqi had not previously demanded payment.

On April 19, 2002, Morikubo Yuji of Japanese Panqi signed the "Decision to Revoke the Letter of Entrustment," deciding to revoke the Letter and its appendices previously executed with Liang Chongxuan, and to revoke Shanghai Panqi, citing serious arrears in payment by Shanghai Panqi to Dalian Panqi and a lack of transparency in its financial and sales activities. On the same day, Dalian Panqi filed a lawsuit with the court against Shanghai Panqi on the grounds of arrears. On April 22 of the same year, Japanese Panqi and Dalian Panqi also issued a "Decision to Revoke the Letter of Entrustment" addressed to Liang Chongxuan individually, and served the decision on Liang Chongxuan on the same day. On the same day, Dalian Panqi issued a "Decision on Revoking Guangdong Panqi Industrial Sales Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Panqi Trading Co., Ltd." to all employees of the sales system, and successively issued an "Urgent Notice" and a "Notice to Customers" to customers, reiterating that Dalian Panqi would no longer authorize Guangdong Panqi or Shanghai Panqi to operate Panqi brand products, and that only Panqi products purchased from Dalian Panqi would carry product liability. In the same month, Dalian Panqi established directly-operated sales offices in Shanghai, Tianjin, and Dongguan to sell its own products. In July, it successively established the Chongqing Office and Qingdao Office for sales activities.

As of April 2002, Shanghai Panqi's investment in establishment and operations (including company setup, software development, and fixed asset acquisitions) amounted to RMB 743,169.25, and its investment in promotional activities (advertising, exhibitions, and other promotional expenses) amounted to RMB 919,597.32, totaling RMB 1,662,766.57.

Shanghai Panqi filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting that Dalian Panqi be ordered to revoke the sales institutions established without Shanghai Panqi's consent, to make a public apology and restore Shanghai Panqi's reputation, to compensate Shanghai Panqi for losses in the amount of RMB 50,000,000, and to bear the litigation costs.

The court of first instance held:

In July 2000, Liang Chongxuan accepted the entrustment of Morikubo Yuji, the legal representative of Japanese Panqi, to specifically establish Shanghai Panqi and gradually build a corresponding marketing network for expanding the sales market of that company and its affiliated enterprises' products in China. In August of the same year, Shanghai Panqi and Dalian Panqi signed the Business Agreement, confirming matters concerning Dalian Panqi's entrustment of Shanghai Panqi for sales in the China region (excluding Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau). This Agreement constituted a commercial entrustment between two independent corporate legal persons. It reflected the true intent of the parties and did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and therefore should be recognized as lawful and valid, binding on the parties. During the performance of the Agreement, Dalian Panqi decided to revoke the original entrusted matters and terminate the Business Agreement for certain reasons, and notified Shanghai Panqi, thereby rendering the termination of the entrustment relationship effective. Because the Business Agreement involved a commercial entrustment, the conclusion and performance of which were based on mutual trust between the parties, once such trust was shaken, in accordance with the provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), either party could terminate the contract, and the principle of specific performance did not apply. Therefore, Dalian Panqi's defense that the Agreement had been lawfully terminated and should not continue to be performed was established, and Shanghai Panqi's claim for continued performance of the Agreement should not be supported. After Dalian Panqi terminated the Agreement and notified Shanghai Panqi in writing, it established corresponding offices, not wholly-owned sales institutions. Its sale of its own products did not violate prohibitive provisions of law. Even if it sold products of other enterprises, that would be a matter for investigation and punishment by relevant administrative authorities and not within the scope of adjustment of this case. Shanghai Panqi invested a certain amount of labor and material resources in performing the Business Agreement, including establishing a company, recruiting personnel, advertising, developing the market, and building a corresponding marketing network. Dalian Panqi's early termination of the Agreement caused certain economic losses to Shanghai Panqi. The termination of the Agreement by Dalian Panqi, which prevented the continued performance of the Agreement, was not attributable to Dalian Panqi. Dalian Panqi should compensate Shanghai Panqi for the economic losses caused by the early termination of the Agreement. Regarding Shanghai Panqi's economic losses, based on the evidence submitted by Shanghai Panqi, the court confirmed them to be RMB 1,662,766.57. Dalian Panqi should compensate Shanghai Panqi for this portion of the losses. Therefore, Shanghai Panqi's claim for compensation for this portion of the losses should be supported. Regarding compensation for expected profit losses, the court held that such losses claimed by Shanghai Panqi were uncertain, and Article 410 of the Contract Law granted the parties to an entrustment contract the right to terminate the contract at any time. Therefore, Shanghai Panqi's claim for expected profit losses after the termination of the contract lacked legal basis and should not be supported. In accordance with Articles 396 and 410 of the Contract Law, the court of first instance ruled:

1. Dalian Panqi shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Shanghai Panqi for the economic losses caused by the termination of the contract in the amount of RMB 1,662,766.07;
2. All other claims of Shanghai Panqi are dismissed.

Court costs for the first instance: RMB 260,010, to be borne by Shanghai Panqi in the amount of RMB 251,429.67 and by Dalian Panqi in the amount of RMB 8,580.33.

Shanghai Panqi, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing:

1. The Business Agreement was a joint venture contract for business division of labor and cooperation, not an entrustment relationship. The judgment of the court of first instance held that during the performance of the Agreement, Dalian Panqi decided to revoke the original entrusted matters and terminate the Business Agreement, and notified Shanghai Panqi, thereby rendering the termination of the entrustment relationship effective. This finding was completely erroneous. The judgment of the court of first instance determined that the Business Agreement constituted a commercial entrustment between two independent corporate legal persons, representing the true intent of the parties and not violating mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and should be recognized as lawful and valid. From this, it inferred that the right to terminate at any time under Article 410 of the Contract Law could simply be applied, allowing unilateral termination. This determination was untenable for the following reasons:

(1) According to the terms of the Business Agreement, the relationship between the parties was one of purchase and sale, a joint venture for business division of labor and cooperation. Article 5 of the Agreement provided: "Party A shall supply products to Party B at the most favorable prices. Detailed matters regarding specific products and prices shall be set forth in separate agreements, which shall be concluded in accordance with the spirit of this Agreement and form an integral part hereof." Article 2 provided: "Party A, as the manufacturing base of the Panqi Group in China, shall supply Party B with the required products. Party B, as the sales representative agency of the Panqi Group in the China region, shall develop the market for the products of the Panqi Group and Party A in the China region." These provisions clearly established that the parties had a buyer-seller relationship as equal entities, i.e., Shanghai Panqi was responsible for selling products and Dalian Panqi was responsible for manufacturing products. This constituted a complete joint venture, not an agency sales entrustment relationship. The provisions of the Agreement regarding the transfer of intangible intellectual property rights also confirmed this point.

(2) The factual existence of the business cooperation joint venture was confirmed. The civil judgment (2003) Hu Gao Min Er Shang Zhong Zi No. 145 of the Shanghai High People's Court determined that since 2000, Dalian Panqi and Shanghai Panqi had engaged in business cooperation, with Shanghai Panqi ordering various molds and accessories from Dalian Panqi by fax and email.

(3) The Business Agreement could not be unilaterally terminated. The Agreement provided: "This Agreement is valid for 20 years, from September 1, 2000 to August 31, 2020. During this period, the parties may negotiate amendments." This clause indicated that the parties had, through the pre-agreed validity period, waived the right of unilateral termination at any time. In accordance with the principle of autonomy of will, this agreement was valid. Even if, as the court of first instance found, it was a commercial entrustment, Dalian Panqi had agreed to waive the right to terminate at any time and therefore could not invoke the provision of Article 410 of the Contract Law that "the principal or the agent may terminate the entrustment contract at any time" and could not unilaterally notify Shanghai Panqi to terminate the Business Agreement. Although the joint venture contract for this cooperative relationship was complex and involved multiple legal relationships, it clearly set forth the rights and obligations of the parties. The Agreement remained valid during the agreed period. The parties must perform the Business Agreement in accordance with the provision that "the parties may negotiate amendments." In the absence of mutual agreement, the original Agreement must continue to be performed.

2. Shanghai Panqi held the sales rights, and Dalian Panqi should cease its breach and perform the contract. The judgment of the court of first instance held that after Dalian Panqi terminated the Agreement and notified Shanghai Panqi in writing, it established corresponding offices, not wholly-owned sales institutions. Its sale of its own products did not violate prohibitive provisions of law. This finding was erroneous. Article 3 of the Business Agreement provided: "Party A entrusts Party B to sell in the China region the products manufactured and operated by Party A. Party A shall not entrust or establish other sales institutions or channels. If necessary, Party A must negotiate an agreement with Shanghai Panqi in advance." Article 6 provided: "Party A shall provide and transfer to Party B free of charge: the sales rights, trademark rights, and other intangible assets in the China region." Since the transfer of sales rights does not require registration or public notice and takes effect upon mutual agreement between the parties, Dalian Panqi agreed to completely abandon its own right to sell and the right to entrust others to sell during the term of the Agreement. Article 5 provided: "Party A shall supply products to Party B at the most favorable prices." In accordance with the above provisions, the Agreement was fully capable of specific performance and must be specifically performed. Once the sales rights were completely and fully transferred, the transferor no longer retained them. The continued performance sought by Shanghai Panqi did not fall within the circumstances under Article 110 of the Contract Law where specific performance is unavailable. Therefore, Dalian Panqi should be ordered to specifically perform.

3. Dalian Panqi should bear full liability for compensation due to non-performance of the contract. The judgment of the court of first instance held that Shanghai Panqi's claim for expected profit losses was uncertain, and Article 410 of the Contract Law granted the parties to an entrustment contract the right to terminate the contract at any time. Therefore, Shanghai Panqi's claim for expected profit losses after termination lacked legal basis and should not be supported. This finding was also erroneous. Article 113 of the Contract Law should apply: "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, and thereby causes losses to the other party, the amount of compensation for losses shall be equivalent to the losses caused by the breach, including the benefits obtainable after the performance of the contract." Therefore, in the absence of special legal provisions or separate agreement by the parties, compensation should be based on the principle of full compensation. The court of first instance incorrectly declined to support the claim for expected profits based on uncertainty and the right to terminate at any time.

4. The circumstances of Dalian Panqi's unilateral breach by terminating the contract were extremely egregious and also demonstrated that it had no direct "right to terminate the entrustment" against Shanghai Panqi. On April 19, 2002, Morikubo Yuji, the legal representative of Dalian Panqi, flew to Shanghai specifically to sign an agreement with Shanghai Panqi on how to continue to successfully conduct sales activities. However, they had already initiated a lawsuit against Shanghai Panqi in Dalian. On April 22 of the same year, the Dalian court immediately sealed Shanghai Panqi's bank accounts. This conduct was a sudden blitzkrieg, a method that would not normally be adopted in normal commercial operations, especially if it were an agency relationship. Therefore, Shanghai Panqi requested that the original judgment be reversed and all of its claims be upheld.

Appellee Dalian Panqi argued in its defense:

1. The judgment of the court of first instance clearly found the facts. In July 2000, Japanese Panqi, through the Decision, authorized and entrusted Shanghai Panqi to build, operate, and manage the Panqi Group's marketing network and to operate and manage sales institutions and channels in the China region. In July of the same year, Japanese Panqi and Liang Chongxuan executed the Letter of Entrustment, entrusting Liang Chongxuan to establish, operate, and manage Shanghai Panqi. In August of the same year, Dalian Panqi and Shanghai Panqi, based on the Letter of Entrustment and the Decision, signed the Business Agreement, which specifically provided for Dalian Panqi's entrustment of Shanghai Panqi to exercise the product sales rights in the China region on its behalf. These agreements were actually performed. Shanghai Panqi had long been in arrears on product sales payments to Dalian Panqi. On April 19, 2002, Japanese Panqi signed the "Decision to Revoke the Letter of Entrustment," terminating its entrustment to Shanghai Panqi and Liang Chongxuan. Liang Chongxuan served as a consultant to Japanese Panqi from December 1, 1999 to December 31, 2001. Liang Chongxuan also served as Deputy General Manager of Dalian Panqi. As of the date of the termination of the contract, Shanghai Panqi's establishment costs, operating expenses, and promotional expenses totaled RMB 1,662,766.57.

2.  The original judgment correctly determined that the Business Agreement constituted an entrustment contract. The Decision, the Power of Attorney, and the Business Agreement in this case constitute a complete and unified set of legal documents by which Dalian Panshi entrusted Shanghai Panshi to exercise the sales rights. The Decision and the Power of Attorney were the prerequisites and principles for the creation of the Business Agreement, while the Business Agreement was the concretization of the Decision and the Power of Attorney. Dalian Panshi first entrusted Liang Chongxuan with the establishment of Shanghai Panshi through the Power of Attorney and the Decision. After the company was established, it further entrusted Shanghai Panshi through the Business Agreement to exercise the sales rights on its behalf and sell its products. The original judgment was correct in comprehensively and systematically examining the interrelationship of the above legal documents, rather than treating any single contract in isolation. The purpose and content of the Business Agreement were to entrust Shanghai Panshi with the exercise of sales rights. As the manufacturer of the products, Dalian Panshi's purpose in concluding the contract was to entrust the sales rights to Shanghai Panshi for exercise to facilitate market development, not merely to sell products to Shanghai Panshi. The collection of goods by Shanghai Panshi from Dalian Panshi was necessary for it to exercise and realize the sales rights; it was not a sale in the market, and therefore cannot negate the character of the Business Agreement as an entrustment contract. The entrusted exercise of sales rights inevitably attached ancillary intellectual property and other civil rights and interests. Dalian Panshi's authorization for Shanghai Panshi to use civil rights such as trademark rights for the products was entirely for the purpose of enabling Shanghai Panshi to exercise and realize the sales rights. This was also determined by the nature of the sales rights themselves and was necessary for the sales conduct. The core issue in dispute between the parties was the termination of the "sales rights." According to principles of civil law, the principal's trust in the agent is the foundation of an entrustment contract. The parties conclude a contract based on trust and terminate it based on a loss of trust. The object of the entrustment in an entrustment contract is a right, which in this case is the product sales right. The entrustment of sales rights must necessarily be connected with sales conduct, intellectual property, and other civil rights and interests.

3.  Shanghai Panshi's grounds for appeal lack factual and legal basis. The Business Agreement in this case is neither a joint venture contract for business division and cooperation nor a sales contract. The General Principles of Civil Law provide for three types of joint ventures: corporate joint ventures, partnership joint ventures, and cooperative joint ventures. There is no single applicable law for cooperative joint venture contracts themselves; they must be governed by the legal provisions applicable to various contracts. The content agreed upon by the parties in the Business Agreement only shows that Dalian Panshi authorized Shanghai Panshi to exercise sales rights, and does not indicate that the agreement constitutes a joint venture contract. The essential content of the Business Agreement in this case is not that Dalian Panshi sold products to Shanghai Panshi, but rather that Dalian Panshi entrusted the exercise of product sales rights to Shanghai Panshi, and Shanghai Panshi sold products within a certain scope based on those sales rights. Shanghai Panshi's equating commercial "business cooperation" with legal joint venture is untenable. Any civil subject concluding a profit-making contract is engaging in some form of business cooperation. However, commercial cooperation does not necessarily mean the parties are engaged in a joint venture. Shanghai Panshi's long-term non-payment for products sold was the cause and reason for Dalian Panshi's termination of the contract. Dalian Panshi terminated the contract in the exercise of its statutory rights; this was not a breach of contract. Therefore, it should not bear liability for damages for breach of contract, and certainly not for losses of prospective profits. The losses resulting from the termination of the contract caused by Shanghai Panshi's own breach should be borne by Shanghai Panshi itself.

In summary, the original judgment found the facts clearly, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the applicable law was correct. However, the conclusion of the original judgment was not comprehensive, as reflected in the following: The original judgment determined that the sales rights had been legally terminated, but failed to rule on the attribution of its ancillary rights. The legal termination of the entrustment contract was caused by Shanghai Panshi's loss of good faith, and its losses should be borne by itself. If the original judgment ordered Dalian Panshi to pay Shanghai Panshi over 1.66 million yuan in compensation for losses caused by the termination of the entrustment contract, then Shanghai Panshi and its sales network should have been awarded to Dalian Panshi. Shanghai Panshi's grounds for appeal are untenable and should be rejected according to law.

This Court, in its second instance, affirms the basic facts found by the original judgment.

Opinion of the Court: This case primarily concerns the nature of the legal relationship between Dalian Panshi and Shanghai Panshi, whether Dalian Panshi has the right to terminate the contract, and whether Shanghai Panshi's claim for loss of prospective profits should be protected.

The Business Agreement signed by Dalian Panshi and Shanghai Panshi in August 2000 stipulated that Dalian Panshi entrusted Shanghai Panshi to sell products manufactured by Dalian Panshi in the China region (excluding Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau); Dalian Panshi, as the manufacturing base of Panshi Group in China, was responsible for supplying the products required by Shanghai Panshi according to the standards of Panshi Group, ensuring quality, timeliness, and quantity; Shanghai Panshi, as the sales representative organization of Panshi Group in the China region, was responsible for developing and expanding the market for Panshi Group and Dalian Panshi products in the China region; Dalian Panshi would supply products at the most favorable prices and would provide and transfer to Shanghai Panshi for free the sales rights, trademark rights, and other intangible assets in the China region; Shanghai Panshi guaranteed the correct use of such sales rights, trademarks, and intangible assets. The above stipulations established an entrustment contract relationship between Dalian Panshi and Shanghai Panshi. The Business Agreement in this case reflects the true intentions of the parties and does not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations; therefore, it should be deemed legal and valid. Shanghai Panshi's ground of appeal that the Business Agreement constitutes a joint venture contract for division and cooperation, not an entrustment relationship, is untenable, and this Court does not support it. An entrustment contract is concluded based on mutual trust between the parties and can also be terminated based on the shaking of that trust foundation. Article 410 of the Contract Law provides: "A principal or an agent may terminate the entrustment contract at any time. If the termination causes losses to the other party, the terminating party shall compensate for the losses, unless the losses are due to reasons not attributable to that party." Dalian Panshi's termination of the entrustment contract relationship with Shanghai Panshi constitutes the exercise of a statutory right of termination. However, this termination caused losses to Shanghai Panshi, and Dalian Panshi shall bear corresponding compensation liability according to law. The original judgment was correct in ordering Dalian Panshi to compensate Shanghai Panshi for the direct losses of RMB 1,662,766.57 (the amount stated as RMB 1,662,766.07 in the original judgment was a clerical error) caused by the termination of the entrustment contract, and this Court affirms that decision.

As for whether Dalian Panshi should also compensate Shanghai Panshi for loss of prospective profits, this Court holds that although a party exercising a statutory right of termination must also bear civil liability, the nature, degree, and consequences of this liability cannot be equated with the liability for breach of contract arising from intentional breach by a party. This case involves civil liability arising from the exercise of a statutory right of termination. Article 410 of the Contract Law provides that a party who causes losses to the other party by terminating an entrustment contract shall bear civil liability for compensating those losses. Based on the nature of the legal relationship in this case and the actual circumstances, it is inappropriate to give an expansive interpretation to "compensation for losses." The original judgment correctly rejected Shanghai Panshi's claim for Dalian Panshi to bear civil liability for loss of prospective profits, and this Court affirms that decision.

In summary, the original judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Shanghai Panshi's grounds for appeal are untenable, and this Court does not support them. Dalian Panshi's request in the second instance to award Shanghai Panshi and its sales network to Dalian Panshi pertains to a separate legal relationship, and as Dalian Panshi's procedural status in this second instance is that of the appellee, this Court will not adjudicate that claim. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby orders as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The court acceptance fee for the second instance, amounting to RMB 260,010, shall be borne by Shanghai Panshi Trade Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Xu Ruibai
Judge: Zhang Shuming
Acting Judge: Zhang Xuemei

November 22, 2005

Clerk: Pan Yongfeng
